metadata.title: Trust, Governance, Safety & Legal Environment Dataset
metadata.description: Comprehensive dataset covering trust in institutions, governance quality, safety, and legal environment for Indonesia, Australia, Italy, Singapore, and Malaysia.
sources: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
OECD Survey on Drivers of Trust in Public Institutions 2024
Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
Gallup World Poll / Pew Research Center 2025
World Bank Doing Business Archive / B-READY 2024

dataPoints.notes: Indonesia consistently ranks among highest globally for government trust; driven by perceived economic progress and national identity
Gallup consistently records high government trust in Indonesia relative to global average of ~43%
Police trust improved after internal reform efforts; still challenged by corruption perceptions at lower levels
Military (TNI) remains one of the most trusted institutions in Indonesia

dataPoints.source: WJP Rule of Law Index 2025 / Gallup
dataPoints.notes: Judicial trust improving but bribery and slow proceedings remain concerns; Constitutional Court more trusted than lower courts
Media trust challenged by political ownership concentration and disinformation concerns
Social media disinformation particularly acute during elections; WhatsApp dominant misinformation vector
Up from 41% prior year; one of the largest year-on-year increases globally. Pew: 'at least half of adults in Indonesia say most people can be trusted'
Business relatively trusted; SOEs hold significant social trust given their role in infrastructure
Below global average of 42. Score has stagnated around 34-38 for a decade. Governance reforms have not translated to measurable CPI gains.
Ranked 109/182 countries. Decline reflects stalled anti-corruption agency (KPK) independence

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Ranks 69/143 countries globally. Strongest factors: order and security. Weakest: absence of corruption, fundamental rights.

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Middle tier globally; improvement from prior years driven by civil justice scores

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Dropped 16 places in 2025 to rank 127/180. Classified as 'difficult situation'. New criminal code enacted 2023 criminalizes criticism of president.

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Fell from 111th in 2024. Key concerns: ITE Law, journalist intimidation in Papua region
Classified as flawed democracy. Electoral process relatively strong; civil liberties and political culture weaker.
Prabowo election 2024 raised concerns about democratic backsliding; military re-involvement in civilian governance
Moderate crime perception. Urban areas like Jakarta have higher crime rates than national average.
Moderate safety perception. Rural areas significantly safer than urban.
One of the lowest homicide rates in Southeast Asia. Note: Indonesia counts offences rather than victims per UNODC methodology notes.
Majority feel safe walking alone at night; significant urban-rural variance

dataPoints.source: UNODC Criminal Justice Resources / Wikipedia List
dataPoints.notes: Polri (national police) only; excludes military police. Coverage uneven across 17,000 islands.
Strict civilian gun control. Effectively near-zero legal civilian ownership. Some estimate 0 per 100.
Death penalty applies to drug trafficking. BNN (National Narcotics Agency) conducts aggressive enforcement. Cannabis: illegal, zero tolerance.

dataPoints.source: Chambers Global Immigration Guide 2024 / ASEAN Briefing
dataPoints.notes: KITAS work permit requires employer RPTKA approval from Ministry of Manpower. Process takes weeks. New 'Second Home Visa' (E33G) improved options for retirees/investors.

dataPoints.source: World Bank B-READY 2024 / Doing Business Archive
dataPoints.notes: World Bank Doing Business discontinued after 2020 fraud controversy. B-READY 2024 covers 50 economies in first release; Indonesia estimated based on prior trend. Significant OSS (Online Single Submission) reforms improved starting a business.

dataPoints.source: IMF/Medina-Schneider Shadow Economy Database; World Economics 2023
dataPoints.notes: Informal sector remains large; agricultural and micro-enterprise sectors predominantly informal. Some estimates reach 30-40% including subsistence.

dataPoints.source: IMF Tax Gap Assessment / DGT Indonesia
dataPoints.notes: VAT compliance improving with e-Faktur digital invoicing system. Corporate tax compliance improving but SME sector largely non-compliant.
Land title system (BPN) improving digitally but disputes remain common. Adat (customary) land rights create legal complexity.

dataPoints.source: USTR Special 301 Report 2024 / US Chamber IP Index 2024
dataPoints.notes: Removed from USTR Priority Watch List in recent years. DJKI increasing enforcement. Mall IP raids ongoing. Software piracy remains high.
Terrorism threats in certain regions (Papua, former Poso area) lower political stability score
Significant improvement from 40th percentile in 2010. Digital governance (OSS, MyASN) driving gains.
Omnibus Law 2020 (Job Creation Law) significantly improved regulatory framework for business
Advanced from 'high' to 'very high' EGDI group in 2024. INA Digital platform driving progress.

dataPoints.source: Law No. 27/2022; CMS Law Oct 2024 briefing
dataPoints.notes: Personal Data Protection Law fully in force from October 17, 2024. GDPR-modeled. Data Protection Authority (Komdigi) being established. Max penalty 2% global turnover.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Classified as 'Partly Free'. New Criminal Code (KUHP) 2023 restricts speech about president, government institutions. ITE Law also restricts online speech.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Political rights: 29/40. Civil liberties: 27/60. Total: 56/100.
Below 50% threshold. Trust erosion linked to housing crisis, cost of living, and climate policy failures.

dataPoints.source: OECD Survey on Drivers of Trust in Public Institutions 2024
dataPoints.notes: Marginally above OECD average. Trust in federal government (46%) lower than trust in public services.

dataPoints.source: OECD Survey on Drivers of Trust 2024 (Australia country note)
dataPoints.notes: Police consistently one of most trusted institutions in Australia. State police forces trusted more than federal agencies.
ADF consistently highly trusted. Defense spending increases under AUKUS have broad support.

dataPoints.source: OECD Survey on Drivers of Trust 2024 (Australia country note)
dataPoints.notes: Courts and judicial system trusted by 59%. Higher than trust in parliament (43%).
Legacy media under pressure. News Corp dominance raises concerns about media pluralism. ABC (public broadcaster) most trusted individual outlet.
Social media distrusted by majority. eSafety Commissioner actively regulates online harms.
High interpersonal trust consistent with other high-income liberal democracies
Business more trusted than government or media. Financial sector trust lower due to 2019 Royal Commission findings.
12th globally. Slight decline from peak of 77 in 2012. Foreign bribery enforcement seen as weak by TI.
Top tier globally. National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) established 2023 to strengthen oversight.

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Ranks 11/143 globally. Strong across all 8 factors. Slight weakness in fundamental rights relative to peers.

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Consistently in top 15 globally

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Ranks 26/180. Generally free press but some concerns about national security law exemptions and journalist surveillance.

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Strong regional leader. No press freedom law or charter; relies on common law protections.
Full democracy. Compulsory voting ensures high electoral participation (>90%).
Ranked in top 15 globally for democracy quality
Moderate crime perception; domestic violence and property crime drive perception. Violent crime low by global standards.
Moderate safety perception; regional and suburban areas much safer than inner cities
Very low homicide rate. Majority domestic-related. Gang-related violence in Melbourne/Sydney clusters.
Majority feel safe at night. Urban pockets (CBD entertainment districts) cited as exceptions.
State police forces plus AFP. Ratio varies: NT highest (~450), NSW lowest (~220).
Post-1996 Port Arthur reforms significantly reduced guns. Numbers slowly recovering through licensed ownership. ~4.2M guns in civilian hands.
ACT decriminalized personal cannabis possession 2020. TGA approved MDMA/psilocybin for therapeutic use 2023. Methamphetamine ('ice') remains primary concern.

dataPoints.source: Home Affairs Department / International Insurance Review 2024
dataPoints.notes: New Skills in Demand Visa (2025) replaced TSS 482 for high earners (AUD 135K+). 7-day processing. Lower-skilled pathways complex and contested.

dataPoints.source: World Bank B-READY 2024 / Doing Business Archive
dataPoints.notes: Very easy to start a business. Online registration through ASIC. Same-day incorporation possible.
Relatively small shadow economy. ATO (tax authority) estimated cash economy gap at AUD 11.3B in 2022.
ATO reports 94%+ voluntary compliance rate for PAYG income tax. Single Touch Payroll system improved compliance since 2018.
Strong Torrens title system. Property rights robustly protected. Land acquisition disputes with Aboriginal title remain sensitive.
IP Australia operates efficiently. Copyright, patent, trademark well enforced. Member of major international IP conventions.
High political stability. Geographic isolation limits external threats. Domestic political stability high despite frequent PM changes 2010-2018.
Top decile globally. Professional public service, high-quality infrastructure, reliable service delivery.
Near top globally. Market-friendly regulations, independent regulators (ASIC, APRA, ACCC).
Top tier globally. myGov platform provides integrated digital government services. Digital ID framework expanding.
Privacy Act 1988 under major reform following 2022 review. Proposed: direct right of action, stronger enforcement, expanded consent requirements. Expected 2025-2026 passage.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Rated Free. Strong civil liberties. No constitutional free speech guarantee but robust common law and statutory protections.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Political rights: 40/40. Civil liberties: 55/60. Slight deductions for Indigenous rights gaps.
Below 50% threshold. Long-standing distrust of central government (stato) particularly in southern Italy. Meloni government initially boosted trust but populist fatigue emerging.

dataPoints.source: OECD Survey on Drivers of Trust in Public Institutions 2024
dataPoints.notes: Below OECD average. Long institutional distrust linked to Tangentopoli legacy, frequent government changes, perceived bureaucratic inefficiency.
Carabinieri and Polizia di Stato relatively trusted, particularly in northern regions. Organized crime infiltration of local police in the south lowers regional trust.
Military trust moderate. Italy's NATO contributions and humanitarian missions maintain positive perception.
Low judicial trust driven by perceived political influence, extremely slow courts (avg trial 7+ years in civil), and Magistrature scandals.
RAI (public broadcaster) under pressure from government influence. Private media highly concentrated (Berlusconi legacy ownership).
Very low social media trust. Italy among EU countries with highest concern about disinformation.
Historically low interpersonal trust; familialism (Banfield 'amoral familism') well-documented in Italian social capital literature. North-South divide: northern Italy ~45%, south ~20%.
Moderate business trust. Family-owned SMEs (PMI) more trusted than large multinationals or banks.
Middle tier for EU. Organized crime (Mafia, Camorra, 'Ndrangheta) impact on public sector remains significant concern.
Lowest CPI score among G7 nations. Public procurement corruption and conflict of interest most cited issues.

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Ranks 31/143. Strong civil justice in principle; extremely slow in practice. Criminal justice more efficient than civil.

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Civil justice factor among lowest in Western Europe due to court delays

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Ranks 48/180. Concerns: journalist intimidation by organized crime, political pressure on RAI, anti-SLAPP cases.

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Meloni government's RAI editorial interference cited by RSF. Below EU median for press freedom.
Classified as flawed democracy. Downgraded from 7.69 (2023). Concerns about judicial independence and media freedom under Meloni.
Fell below 'full democracy' threshold. Italy is the only G7 country classified as flawed democracy.
Moderate crime perception. Significant variance: Milan/Rome score higher; smaller cities much safer.
Moderate safety. Petty crime (pickpocketing in tourist areas) main concern rather than violent crime.
Very low homicide rate. Mafia-related killings historically concentrated in Sicily, Calabria, Campania; all declining long-term.

dataPoints.source: Gallup Law and Order Report 2024 / Eurobarometer
dataPoints.notes: Majority feel safe at night in Italy overall. Significant variance by city and region.
Very high police density. Four national police forces: Polizia di Stato, Carabinieri, Guardia di Finanza, Polizia Penitenziaria. Historically high relative to crime rates.
Moderate civilian gun ownership for Europe. Hunting culture sustains licensed ownership. Strict licensing required.
Cannabis decriminalized for personal use but not legal. Cocaine prevalent in northern cities. Heroin problem historically significant in certain regions.
Bureaucratic immigration process. Decreto Flussi (annual immigration quota) oversubscribed. Click Day system for seasonal workers criticized for chaos. EU Blue Card available for high-skilled.

dataPoints.source: World Bank Doing Business Archive 2020 / OECD PMR 2024
dataPoints.notes: Bureaucratic burden historically very high. Simplified company registration (SRL semplificata) and digital SPID/Fascicolo aziendale reforms improving outlook.
ISTAT officially estimates 'economia non osservata' at ~10-12% but broader shadow economy estimates reach 21%. Southern Italy significantly higher.
MEF estimates annual tax gap at EUR 84B. VAT gap improving with e-invoicing (fatturazione elettronica) mandatory since 2019. Self-employed compliance historically poor.
Moderate property rights. Slow eviction processes for non-paying tenants creates investment risk. Anti-mafia asset confiscation well-organized.

dataPoints.source: US Chamber IP Index 2024 / European Commission
dataPoints.notes: Strong IP laws; enforcement variable. Counterfeit goods (particularly luxury sector) remain significant issue. Specialised IP tribunals established.
Political stability moderate. Italy has had 70+ governments since 1946. Current Meloni government unusually stable by Italian standards.
Moderate-good government effectiveness. PNRR implementation improving state capacity. North-South public administration quality gap very significant.
Regulatory quality improving with PNRR reforms. Competition authority (AGCM) independent and active.
Good e-government development. SPID digital identity, PagoPA payment platform, IO app driving improvements. PNRR funding EUR 6.7B for digital transition.
Full GDPR compliance as EU member. Garante per la Protezione dei Dati Personali (DPA) is one of EU's most active: blocked ChatGPT March 2023, issued large fines to Meta, Google.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Still rated Free but declining (-2 from prior year). RAI editorial independence concerns, anti-SLAPP defamation suits against journalists.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Classified Free but with noted concerns about Meloni government's media relationship and anti-NGO sentiment
Consistently high government trust globally. PAP dominance and technocratic governance drive trust. Recent Lee family dispute slightly dented institutional trust.

dataPoints.source: Singapore Police Force Public Perception Survey 2024
dataPoints.notes: Exceptionally high police trust. SPF maintains world-class community policing. Zero-tolerance enforcement builds confidence.
SAF highly trusted. National Service (NS) mandatory for all male citizens builds broad institutional familiarity and trust.

dataPoints.source: WJP Rule of Law Index 2025 / Gallup
dataPoints.notes: Very high judicial trust. Singapore courts are efficient, independent, and corruption-free. International commercial arbitration hub (SIAC).
State-linked SPH Media dominates. POFMA (fake news law) actively used to correct perceived misinformation. Media seen as reliable but government-aligned.
POFMA law creates risk for false social media posts. Government actively counters disinformation online.
Paradoxically moderate interpersonal trust despite high institutional trust. Multi-ethnic society with some in-group vs out-group dynamics. Collective harmony emphasis over spontaneous trust.
High business trust driven by rule-of-law environment, low corruption, and business-friendly regulation. GLC (government-linked companies) generally trusted.
3rd globally. Consistently one of the least corrupt nations. CPIB (Corruption Practices Investigation Bureau) extremely effective deterrent.
Top 3 globally alongside Denmark and Finland. High civil servant salaries aligned to private sector reduce corruption incentive.

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Ranks 17/143. Strong in order, security, civil justice, absence of corruption. Lower scores in fundamental rights, open government (civil society restrictions).

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: High globally but lower than CPI rank (3rd) due to fundamental rights and open government restrictions

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Ranks 123/180. POFMA law, defamation suits against critics, state media dominance drive low score. Government disputes RSF methodology.

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Low press freedom globally despite high development. POFMA (Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act) central concern.
Flawed democracy. PAP has governed since 1959; opposition constrained but growing. GRC electoral system favors incumbents.
Strong on electoral process and functioning government; weak on civil liberties and political culture diversity
One of the lowest crime indices in the world. Strict deterrent laws (caning, mandatory minimums) historically effective.
Among world's safest cities. SPF annual crime statistics show consistently low total crime.

dataPoints.source: UNODC / Singapore Police Force Annual Report 2023
dataPoints.notes: Extremely low homicide rate. Among world's 10 lowest. Zero gang murders in most years.
Near-universal perception of safety. One of highest globally.

dataPoints.source: Singapore Police Force Annual Statistics 2023 / govinsider.asia
dataPoints.notes: Very high police density for a city-state. SPF supplemented by NSmen police NS commitments.
Near-zero civilian gun ownership. Firearms Act prohibits civilian ownership except licensed gun clubs and specific roles.
Death penalty mandatory for trafficking above threshold quantities (e.g., 15g heroin). Cannabis: illegal, zero tolerance, life imprisonment for trafficking.

Employment Pass (EP) requires minimum SGD 5,000/month salary (SGD 5,500 for financial sector). COMPASS points-based system introduced 2023. Tightening to protect locals (Fair Consideration Framework).
Tops global rankings for business environment. Singapore, Denmark, US lead B-READY 2024. Incorporation in 1-2 days via BizFile+.
Smallest shadow economy among the 5 countries. High compliance culture, electronic payments widespread, IRAS efficiency.
IRAS reports 99%+ voluntary compliance for corporate income tax. No capital gains tax, no estate duty simplifies compliance.
2nd globally. Physical property rights: 8.25. Very strong legal/political environment for property. Leasehold (99-year HDB) model dominant.
Among global top 5 for IP protection. IPOS is innovative. Singapore is regional IP hub. IP courts specialized and efficient.
Exceptionally stable. No significant terrorism risk; political succession managed orderly.
Top 1% globally for government effectiveness. Meritocratic civil service, data-driven governance, world-class infrastructure.
Best globally for regulatory quality. Pro-business, clear, consistently enforced regulations.
Top 3 globally. SingPass/MyInfo platform is global model for digital identity. Smart Nation initiative comprehensive.
PDPA 2020 amendment: max fine raised to 10% of annual Singapore turnover (for turnover >SGD 10M). PDPC active enforcement. Data portability and data innovation provisions added.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Classified Partly Free. POFMA, ISA (Internal Security Act), defamation laws restrict speech. PAP uses legal mechanisms to constrain political opponents.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Political rights: 19/40. Civil liberties: 29/60. The gap between governance quality and political freedom is a defining Singapore paradox.
Anwar Ibrahim government (since 2022) raised trust with anti-corruption rhetoric. 1MDB scandal aftermath still weighs on institutional trust.
Ipsos: two-thirds believe police treat everyone equally. Up from lower levels post-2019 IPCMC debates. Police reform ongoing.
ATM (Angkatan Tentera Malaysia) trusted by clear majority across ethnic groups
Improving post-Najib conviction. Independence questions under previous administrations; current trajectory positive.
Government-linked media conglomerates (Utusan, Media Prima, Astro) dominate. Media freedom improving but political ownership prevalent.
Social media significant political battlefield in Malaysia. MCMC actively censors content deemed seditious or harmful.
Among the lowest globally per Ipsos. Multi-ethnic society with racial trust dynamics (Malay, Chinese, Indian communities). Structural ethnic divisions reduce generalized trust.
Business trusted by majority. Bumiputera equity policies create perception of uneven playing field among non-Malay communities.
Ranked 54th. Improving from low of 47 (2018 1MDB era). Najib conviction and MACC strengthening signal progress.
Best ASEAN non-Singapore rank alongside Brunei. Post-1MDB recovery ongoing; patronage networks persist.

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Ranks 51/143. Improving trajectory. Stronger than Indonesia but below Singapore. Civil justice accessible; criminal justice reforms ongoing.

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Significant improvement from 61st in 2022. Judiciary reform under Anwar government cited.

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Jumped from 107th to 88th in 2025. RSF cites reduced journalist prosecutions under Anwar government. Sedition Act still a concern.

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Best ASEAN rank excluding Timor-Leste. 19-place jump from 107th in 2024. Political will to reform evident.
Highest ASEAN score (flawed democracy). Electoral process improving; civil liberties still constrained by Sedition Act, SOSMA, etc.
Best democracy ranking in ASEAN (excluding Singapore which scores lower on civil liberties). Competitive elections now well-established.
Moderate-high crime perception. Snatch theft and property crime main concerns. Organized crime (secret societies/triads) historically present.
Moderate safety perception. KL perceived less safe than Penang or smaller cities.
Higher than regional peers (Singapore 0.2, Indonesia 0.4). Drug-related and gang violence contribute. Declining from 3.1 per 100k in 2010.
Slight majority feel safe at night. Women's safety perception notably lower than men's.
PDRM (Royal Malaysian Police). High density. Under-staffed in rural East Malaysia (Sabah/Sarawak) despite national high average.
Low civilian gun ownership. Police and security companies licensed. Illegal firearms problem linked to cross-border smuggling (Philippines corridor).

Mandatory death penalty for drug trafficking; 2023 reform allows judges discretion for cooperating defendants. Opioid substitution therapy available. Drug abuse treated as public health issue alongside enforcement.
Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) visa reformed 2023 (stricter financial requirements). Employment Pass for professionals streamlined. DE Rantau digital nomad visa launched 2022.

dataPoints.source: World Bank Doing Business 2020 (last full data) / SSM Malaysia
dataPoints.notes: Historically strong (ranked 12 in 2020 for starting a business). SSM online incorporation streamlined. Companies Act 2016 modernized framework.
Large informal sector particularly in construction and low-skilled labor (migrant workers). GST reintroduction debate linked to formalization goals.
SST compliance improving post-GST abolition (2018). E-invoicing mandatory from 2024 for large businesses, 2025 for SMEs. Tax-to-GDP ratio low (~12%) reflecting compliance gaps.
Moderate property rights. Land title system functional. Bumiputera property quotas create complexity for foreign investors. Strata titles reform ongoing.
Disabled 2,000+ piracy websites 2023. Malaysia removed from USTR Watch List. IP court established. Counterfeit goods still prevalent in Petaling Street and online.
Political stability improving post-2022 coalition government formation. Repeated elections 2018-2022 were destabilizing; current government more durable.
Good government effectiveness. Civil service professional but influenced by political appointments and ethnic quota policies.
Good regulatory quality. New Industrial Master Plan 2030 aims to attract advanced manufacturing. ESG regulations tightening.
2nd in Southeast Asia behind Singapore. MyDigital initiative driving rapid digitization. MyEG, MySejahtera (pandemic) platforms exemplify capability.
PDPA 2010 being comprehensively amended; major changes effective June 2025. New National Guidelines on AI Governance introduced Sept 2024. Mandatory breach notification coming.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Partly Free. Sedition Act (1948) still in force. MCMC blocks content. Anwar government less aggressive with critics than predecessors. Growing civil society space.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Political rights: 22/40. Civil liberties: 31/60. Total: 53/100. Improving trend under current government.
Singapore best, Indonesia worst among 5. Singapore 3rd globally; Indonesia 109th globally.

dataPoints.source: World Justice Project Rule of Law Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Australia leads; Indonesia lowest. Italy notably lower than CPI/development level suggests due to slow civil justice.

dataPoints.source: Reporters Without Borders Press Freedom Index 2025
dataPoints.notes: Australia clearly leads. Singapore and Indonesia both in 'difficult situation' category. Malaysia rapidly improving.
Australia only full democracy. All others flawed. Singapore scores lower than Indonesia on this index despite superior governance metrics.
Singapore dramatically safer in perception. Others cluster at moderate safety. Malaysia lowest.
All 5 countries have very low homicide rates globally. Malaysia notably higher than others in group.

dataPoints.source: Freedom House Freedom in the World 2025
dataPoints.notes: Australia and Italy rated Free; others Partly Free. Singapore lowest in group despite being most economically developed.
Singapore global top 3. All 5 countries in 'Very High' EGDI group. Indonesia recently entered Very High tier.
Singapore and Australia have smallest shadow economies. Malaysia surprisingly high despite development level.

dataPoints.source: Pew Research Center 2025 / Ipsos / WVS Wave 7
dataPoints.notes: Malaysia and Italy have surprisingly low interpersonal trust. Indonesia rising fast. Australia high as expected for high-trust society.
Inverse correlation with press freedom: countries with least media freedom have highest government trust. Indonesia highest despite lowest corruption/rule of law scores.
